title: The Rookery on the Ice Cliff
story: Thrimwald the Rookery Chill is a creeping frost that slides along the glacier cliff, freezing the north ledge of the snow-gull rookery solid. The gulls beg Mr 6 to move the threatened hatchlings to the sunny south ledge before the chill arrives, and he has a stack of little wicker sleds to do it with.
question: There are 320 hatchlings in the rookery, and 5/8 of them sit on the north ledge Thrimwald is freezing. Each wicker sled carries 24 hatchlings. How many sleds does Mr 6 need to move all the north-ledge hatchlings?
solution: 200 ÷ 24 = 8 remainder 8, and those last 8 hatchlings still need a ride.
praise: Finding the fraction and then dividing was exactly the right plan — the last step was rounding UP, because 8 leftover hatchlings still need a sled of their own.
hint: First figure out how many hatchlings are actually on the north ledge, then think about what happens to the ones left over after the full sleds are loaded.
victory: Nine sleds whooshed down the ice chute, the last one carrying just eight squeaky hatchlings and one very pleased knight. Thrimwald froze an empty ledge, sighed a frosty sigh, and drifted off to freeze something less clever.
imagePrompt: A numeral-six knight in a blue cape loading fluffy snow-gull hatchlings onto wicker sleds on a glowing blue glacier ledge as a pale creeping frost-shape slides toward them under a rose-colored arctic sky.
